transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I go from feeling like I can work nonstop and take on everything to suddenly having no energy to even show up for my shifts. My manager and my mom got really worried about how back-and-forth I've been, so I agreed to come in and get checked out.
During the times when you can work nonstop, have you also felt unusually high or irritable, needed much less sleep, or been more impulsive than usual? About how long do those periods usually last?

During those highs, I feel on top of the world and stay up all night working on business plans without needing any rest, but I also get really irritable and snap at people over minor things. That intense period lasted for about a month before I crashed into this low state, which has been going on for the last three months.
During that month-long high period, did you ever have hallucinations or fixed beliefs that others said weren’t true, or did things get severe enough that you were hospitalized?

No, I've never had any hallucinations or believed things that other people told me weren't true or impossible. It never got so bad that I had to go to the hospital, either. I just felt really revved up and convinced I could do it all.

Since the low period started, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day, with loss of interest in things you usually enjoy? Have you also had changes in sleep or appetite, trouble concentrating, feelings of worthlessness, or thoughts of death or suicide?

Yeah, I've completely lost interest in soccer and cooking, and I feel constantly exhausted no matter how much I sleep. My brain is so foggy that I forget customer orders, and my appetite is a mess—I'll go all day without eating and then inhale a whole pizza at midnight. I don't have any thoughts of suicide or self-harm, but everything just feels completely pointless and draining right now.
During this 3-month low period, have you also been feeling worthless or excessively guilty nearly every day? If yes, can you give one example?
No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling worthless or guilty. It's more that I just feel completely drained of energy and like everything is pointless, rather than feeling down on myself in that way.

During that month when you felt high and needed little sleep, did your behavior cause serious problems, like getting fired, spending a lot of money, risky sex, legal trouble, or people saying you were acting way out of character?

Yes, it definitely caused some major issues. My mom got really worried about my extreme energy shifts, and my manager pulled me aside for erratic performance and because I was talking to him like I knew more than him. I also fell behind on my rent and bills, and I really strained my reputation as a reliable mentor to the newer staff.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a clear prior manic episode lasting about 1 month with elevated/irritable mood, markedly decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, and significant functional impairment, followed by a current major depressive episode lasting 3 months with anhedonia, fatigue, concentration problems, appetite disturbance, hypersomnia, and pervasive pointlessness. There are no psychotic symptoms. This is most consistent with bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic without psychotic symptoms, given the bipolar diagnosis is established by the manic episode history and the only candidate provided is F31.1.
